entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pere Antoni Beuter (c. 1490–1554) was a Spanish historian, chronicler, and humanist, primarily active in Valencia, whose monumental *Crónica general de España* became a foundational text for Spanish national historiography in the early modern period. His work synthesized medieval chronicles with Renaissance humanism, aiming to provide a comprehensive narrative of the Iberian Peninsula from its mythical origins to his own time, thereby contributing significantly to the construction of a distinct Valencian and broader Spanish identity. Beuter's meticulous research and narrative skill positioned him as a key figure in the transition from medieval annalistic writing to more structured, critical historical scholarship.

Beuter's magnum opus, the *Crónica general de España*, first published in 1538 and later expanded, systematically traced the history of Spain through various kingdoms, rulers, and significant events, often drawing upon classical sources like Strabo and Livy, alongside medieval Iberian chronicles. He notably incorporated detailed accounts of the Aragonese Crown and the Kingdom of Valencia, elevating their historical importance within the broader Spanish narrative. Beyond his historical writings, Beuter also authored works on heraldry and genealogy, such as *La primera parte de la Coronica general de toda España* (1538), and a *Primera parte de la historia de Valencia* (1546), demonstrating his wide-ranging intellectual interests and commitment to documenting regional histories. His work was particularly influential for its attempt to reconcile mythological origins, like the Hercules legend, with more verifiable historical data.
